questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Elite university, located in the United Kingdom, small town which allowed fuller immersion into student life, old town with beautiful architecture and many traditions.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Assuming 10 is best.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The university team is super helpful and it is clear that this is a university with a lot of resources. Quick answers to emails, accessible lecturers/professors and much more.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I hade quite a number of email corresondance. Other than that I was helped in general by university employees in various other instances where it was required.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Assuming 5 is best.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The University of St Andrews does not follow a campus-system, as far as I know. Therefore I do not see the relevence of this question. I applied to university accommodation, which I believe is guaranteed to incoming exchange students. So I wholeheartedly recommend applying for it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Applying for university accommodation is as I see it the far best option. Catered, if possible. It allows for immersion into student life much more. Keep in mind that university accommodation is guaranteed for all first-year students. Thus, the people living in the halls are often 18-20 years old, which is often younger than exchange students from Copenhagen. I managed to find a large group of friends even though we had age differences.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Assuming 5 is best.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Assuming 5 is best.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find courses before hand and apply for them, as I remember it. In Fresher's week or the equivalent for semester 2, we had to go to a building and to talk to person about our choices and they made sure we had the prerequisites to take the courses we had chosen. Super easy and smooth process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the help one can imagine.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One class was not available that I wanted but I easily found another. It was no issue.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really any. It is very straight forward and should not require any help, I think.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Assuming 5 is best.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were challenging. I took courses meant for 4th yeas while I was a 3rd year. I recommend going a year up in course levels.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much the same. Tutorials are set up in the a way such that you have to do the problems before coming to class but other than that it was more or less the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: EC4432 - Development and Finance was the best course I have ever taken at a university. The lecturer, Mr Saxena, is one of the best teachers I have had. Interesting module with challenging articles to read, a brilliant essay to write which offers great flexibility. Cannot recomment it enough.

Housing DKK per month *

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you are in catered accommodation then there really is no extra costs, other than insurance and personal consumption. Books for class can easily be lent at the library for the whole semester. Public transport is quite expensive though, so if you plan on trips in Scotland while being there, just know about the cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Pints are cheap. Meal-deal with Tesco club card is just brilliant for the price.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a society for everything.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything one can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of sport societies and cultural societies (i.e. German society, Swiss society etc.) that present an excellent opportunity to meet different people at the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Have fun. Go to Aikman's cellar. Go hiking in the Highlands. Dundee is also an interesting weekend one-day destination. Loads of things to do.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get catered accommodation. Meals in the hall was my main source of meeting people in St Andrews.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: American political correctness and a British culture of surveilence and more "nannying" from the University.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most parts about the culture at St Andrews I liked very much. Keep in mind something like 30% of the student body is American.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Meet people, even though they might be a little younger than yourself. Get catered accommodation and go to the meals in the halls. Go see a bit of Scotland if you have time. The Highlands are beutiful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: YoungScot Card for free bus travel if under 23, Tesco Club Card for cheaper stuff in Tesco.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any challenges. The semesters are quite short to there's that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was an amazing experience. Cannot recommend St Andrews enough.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
